clue.text: 9 19 No 1 with spy working in cyberspace

definitions.note: entries 9 and 19 together spell the narrator's married name, so No 1 is the first wife to hold it

indicators.note: working signals that letters are being rearranged: the answer plus the word spy, reworked, give the letters of cyberspace

explanation.surface: An intelligence agent operating online, hacking away in cyberspace.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer with SPY, shuffled ('working'), gives the letters of CYBERSPACE.
explanation.definitionFit: In the du Maurier novel the title character is Maxim de Winter's first, dead wife.

clue.text: This French writer of note ruined PhD — the making of Daphne du Maurier …

indicators.note: the making of means the answer plus the words ruined PhD rearranged form the author's full name

explanation.surface: A French author whose failed doctorate launched du Maurier's career.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer plus RUINED PHD, rearranged ('the making of'), gives DAPHNE DU MAURIER. 'writer of note' means a composer, not an author.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Philippe Rameau was an eighteenth-century French composer, someone who writes musical notes.

clue.text: … American press on supporting British admirer of George

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue means the following pieces sit beneath the letter above

parts.note: hie is an old verb meaning hurry or press on

explanation.surface: American media back a British fan of George.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' works because this is a down clue: the supporting pieces sit beneath B. George is George W. Bush.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter of President George W. Bush was dubbed by this nickname.

clue.text: Conventional bridge tactic induced big slams

indicators.note: slams means hits or bashes, so the words are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A standard bridge ploy that led to big slam contracts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slams' looks like bridge jargon, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, a conventional bid in a new suit that shows a control, such as an ace, when exploring slam.

clue.text: See 12
Like du Maurier's The Birds, breaking chain

indicators.note: breaking means one piece is split open by the other piece set within it

parts.note: ch is the abbreviation for the chain, an old unit of length of 22 yards
ornis is a collective term for the birds of a region, its avifauna

explanation.surface: A remark that du Maurier's story The Birds is like a chain being snapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Birds' looks like the du Maurier title, but it is ORNIS (a region's bird life) inside CH, the abbreviation for the old surveying chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Daphne du Maurier lived in and wrote about Cornwall, so her stories belong to that county.

clue.text: Relief for suffering fan sealing last passage on top of Menabilly

indicators.note: sealing means enclosing, so one piece shuts the others inside

parts.note: to fan is to cool by moving air

indicators.note: on in a down clue means placed above the next piece

parts.note: a coda is the final section of a piece of music

indicators.note: top of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Relief for a suffering admirer: the final scene set at Menabilly, du Maurier's home.
explanation.walkthrough: COOL ('fan') is 'sealing' CODA and M. Menabilly was du Maurier's Cornish house.
explanation.definitionFit: A common painkiller combining codeine and paracetamol, taken for relief from pain.

clue.text: Castle Dor missing introduction about fair

indicators.note: about means the remaining letters are turned round
missing introduction means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: OK means fair, middling, all right

explanation.surface: A du Maurier novel title, Castle Dor, about a fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Castle Dor' reads as the du Maurier novel, but Castle is the definition, the chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess the castle is another name for this piece.

clue.text: Papers covering artistic setting in Cornwall after the writer's done copy

indicators.note: after means the next piece follows the first

parts.note: the writer's is read as the writer is, the setter saying I'm

indicators.note: covering means one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: ID means identity papers
Tate St Ives is the Tate art gallery in Cornwall

explanation.surface: Documents at a Cornish arts venue after the author has finished copying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' puts the papers round the gallery (Tate St Ives in Cornwall), and 'after' places that behind the setter's 'I am'.
explanation.definitionFit: Having produced a copy, one has copied or mimicked something.

clue.text: Pause is at The Breaking Point

indicators.note: breaking means smashing up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A pause before reaching The Breaking Point, du Maurier's story collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Breaking Point' reads as the du Maurier title, but 'Breaking' rearranges IS AT THE plus E for east.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold back in doubt is to pause, waver, or hang back before acting.

clue.text: See 25
Fish swimming in cave round House on the Strand's head

indicators.note: round means the scrambled letters go around the next piece
swimming suggests movement, so the letters of in cave are mixed up
head of a word means its opening letter

explanation.surface: Fish swimming in a cave near the place in du Maurier's The House on the Strand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' turns IN CAVE into ANCVIE, which goes 'round' HO; then add S, the 'head' of Strand's.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small, salty fish of the herring family, often tinned or used on pizza.

clue.text: Timeless stories, as put about by the same devotee

indicators.note: put about means the outer letters are placed around the shortened stories

parts.note: read as the plural of the letter A: two As

indicators.note: timeless means the letter T (time) is taken out

parts.note: stories collectively are fiction
T is the abbreviation for time
do is short for ditto, meaning the same again

explanation.surface: A fan admires stories without a timestamp, repeated to the same reader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is read as 'A's', two letters A, which are 'put about' the stories with 'Timeless' removing T for time.
explanation.definitionFit: An enthusiast or keen fan of an activity, from the Spanish word for a lover of bullfighting.

clue.text: Novel start: enter woman, imagining deathly detail

definitions.text: Novel start: enter woman, imagining deathly detail

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters that follow are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A description of how a book opens: a woman appears, dreaming of morbid particulars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' is both the anagram signal and the subject: all of the other words are shuffled, and the whole clue describes the famous dream that opens du Maurier's book.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the celebrated opening sentence of Rebecca, the narrator dreaming of the ruined Cornish house.

clue.text: Aspects I see represented over top of York?

definitions.text: Aspects I see represented over top of York?

indicators.note: over means the rearranged letters sit across and around the next piece

parts.note: see sounds like the letter C

indicators.note: represented means shown afresh, so the letters are presented in a new arrangement
top of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone describing the views they see from high above York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' rearranges ASPECTS I and C (from see); that goes 'over' Y, the 'top of' York. The whole clue also describes urban views.
explanation.definitionFit: Views of a town or its skyline, such as those from York Minster tower, are urban panoramas.

clue.text: See 12
Means to uplift sea lover, moved with impression of Troy

indicators.note: moved means shifted around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for troy, the system of weights, an abbreviation being a short impression of the word

explanation.surface: A sea lover is moved by an image of ancient Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' rearranges SEA LOVER plus T, the abbreviation for troy weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifts carry people up between floors, so they are devices for raising.

clue.text: With bands announced, follower of Q is not half engrossed

indicators.note: engrossed means absorbed, so pieces are taken in by the outer word

parts.note: stated means said or announced
in the alphabet R comes right after Q

indicators.note: not half means only one of the two letters is kept

explanation.surface: A band's follower, with Q in the crowd, is not half absorbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'announced' looks like a homophone signal, but it is STATED, which has 'engrossed' R (after Q) and I (half of is).
explanation.definitionFit: Marked with parallel lines or stripes, as rock or muscle can be.

clue.text: Just a little boy swallowing a fly

indicators.note: swallowing means one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: a son is a boy
a midge is a small fly

explanation.surface: Echoes the nursery rhyme about swallowing a fly, here a little lad.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny amount, a variant spelling of smidgen.

clue.text: See 12
See 25
See 12
Characters at back of Old Ferry Inn I misguidedly race

indicators.note: misguidedly means the letters picked are sent the wrong way, mixed up
characters at back of each word are their final letters

explanation.surface: Someone at an old ferry pub wrongly running a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters at back of' takes D, Y, N and I, the final letters of Old, Ferry, Inn and I; 'misguidedly' rearranges DYNI.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for the Indianapolis 500, the American motor race run each May.

clue.text: Top producer of dramatic works drinks mid-morning?

parts.note: a cap is a top, such as the lid of a bottle
Puccini was the Italian composer of operas such as Tosca and La Boheme

explanation.surface: A leading playwright has a coffee break during the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'dramatic works' are operas, not plays; the question mark marks the definition as an example rather than a dictionary sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Frothy milky coffees are a typical mid-morning order, so these are drinks for that time of day.

clue.text: Heading for Polmear, load up bike

indicators.note: heading for means the opening letter of the next word
up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to lade is to load a ship

explanation.surface: Setting off for Polmear in Cornwall, loading up the bike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading for' gives P, and 'up' turns LADE ('load') round in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride a bicycle is to push its foot levers round, so the verb means cycle.

clue.text: Summer for French crowned by the start of Fowey Festival

indicators.note: crowned by in a down clue means the previous letter sits on top
the start of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: ete is the French word for summer

explanation.surface: French summer visitors topped by a festival at Fowey, du Maurier's Cornish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crowned by' puts F, 'the start of' Fowey, above ETE in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A local outdoor fair or gala, often to raise money for a church or school.

clue.text: No 2 gutted Manchester team to sack one during next season

indicators.note: during means the pieces go within the phrase made of the other two parts

parts.note: the next one after number one is two, given as an ordinal phrase
one of the four seasons: the coldest

indicators.note: gutted means the inside is removed, leaving only the outer letters
to sack means to get rid of, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: a side is a team in football or cricket
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A football manager wants the deputy to fire a player in next season's Manchester squad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' keeps only the outer letters, 'to sack' drops I from the team, and 'during' sets both inside the phrase made by next (as an ordinal) and season.
explanation.definitionFit: In Rebecca the unnamed narrator is Maxim's second wife, so she is number two after Rebecca.

clue.text: Tense chapter after close of Jamaica Inn describes plot

indicators.note: describes in its geometric sense of drawing around, so one piece encloses the rest

parts.note: PH is the abbreviation for public house, an inn

indicators.note: after means the following pieces come later in the order
close of a word means its final letter

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A tense chapter set after the end of Jamaica Inn tells of a plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jamaica Inn' is a du Maurier title, but here 'close of' takes A from Jamaica, and Inn is PH (public house), which 'describes' (goes round) A, T and C.
explanation.definitionFit: A small piece of ground, as in a vegetable bed, is another word for a plot.

clue.text: Housekeeper's high and barely mighty

definitions.note: the possessive reads as housekeeper is, naming the character

indicators.note: high as in drunk or intoxicated signals the letters are muddled
barely, as in stripped bare, means the outer letters are removed

parts.note: mighty in its informal adverb sense means very, ever so

explanation.surface: The housekeeper is lofty and only just powerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' (drunk) muddles the word and; 'barely' strips the outer letters from EVER SO, informal 'mighty' as in mighty fine. 'High and mighty' reads as one phrase but is split.
explanation.definitionFit: Mrs Danvers is the sinister housekeeper at Manderley in du Maurier's novel.

clue.text: Set sail with du Maurier's ultimate former model

indicators.note: set means arranged in a new way, so the letters are reorganised
ultimate means the final letter of the surname, before the possessive

explanation.surface: Setting sail with the final work of du Maurier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' rearranges SAIL, DU and R, the final letter of Maurier.
explanation.definitionFit: Linda Lusardi was a well-known British glamour model of the 1980s, now retired from that career.
